name: settle
purpose: The house curve. Row expands (grid-rows 0fr→1fr), chevron rotation on the same token, fades and panel swaps. This is the motion the founder singled out by name from 053 (PO-1038 · Bodega Álvaro); carried forward unchanged.

name: ink
purpose: Micro-states: hovers, borders, chip fills, the theme switch, the kicker numeral recolouring when the seal changes. Nothing moves more than 2px.

name: tuck
purpose: Objects that move under a finger — toggle thumbs, drawer handles, swipe returns. Near-critically damped: measured 1% overshoot, which reads as weight rather than as bounce.

name: turn
purpose: “Show the working” — the page-turn reveal for arithmetic panes, vendor-thread drawers and history. Slower than settle on purpose: this one opens a record, so it should feel like turning to a page rather than flicking a row.

name: press
purpose: Hold-to-approve. The fill is deliberately linear because the operator is timing it against their own thumb; the cancel/release uses the house curve. One deliberate gesture replaces a confirm dialog, and nothing auto-sends.

name: stamp
purpose: The seal landing on an approved entry. The single emphatic motion in the system and the only place overshoot is permitted (measured 11%), because entering something into the book deserves a small ceremony and nothing else does.

name: tally
purpose: Number tickers on KPI cells and stock counts. Overdamped, 0% overshoot — figures arrive, they never bounce past and correct themselves. durationMs is time to within 1% of target on a $4,280 run; fully at rest at 1408ms.

name: shimmer
purpose: The AI thinking sweep across serif-italic text (“Totting up the night…”) and across the “AI draft ready” chip. Replaces every spinner in the product; it is the only motion the AI is allowed while working.

name: stagger
purpose: Entrance interval for KPI tiles and list rows. First paint only — never on re-render, never on filter or sort, because a list that re-staggers on every keystroke is noise.
